entries.verdict_line: Bank Nifty at a 97th-percentile high while corporate bond issuance hits a 7th-percentile panic print — the market is pricing banking strength that the funding structure cannot sustain.
Copper at $6.63 — a 79th-percentile print — and iron ore at $161.91 both rising while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR: industrial metals are pricing a recovery the data refuses to confirm.
Nikkei at a 100th-percentile high while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — global equities are pricing a recovery that the underlying economy has not yet written.
India VIX at a 7th-percentile low while airline passengers collapse to a 7th-percentile low — complacency and consumption are cracking in unison, and the market hasn't noticed.

US 10Y at 4.69% — an 84th-percentile yield while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — is repricing every carry trade that funded EM inflows; India's FII reversal from +₹22,615 cr to -₹114 cr in a single period is the first tremor.
Natural gas at a 15th-percentile low cuts India's LNG import bill — but airline passengers at a 7th-percentile collapse say the consumer funding that bill is already spent.
Gold in INR at an all-time ₹13,472/gram while SIP accounts grow at a 2nd-percentile crawl — India's savers are fleeing paper assets faster than new investors are entering them.
Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile high while eurozone GDP prints 0.9% — European equities are pricing a prosperity the continent's output has not earned.
Bank Nifty at a 95th-percentile high while FII equity flows swung ₹22,729 cr negative in a single period — the market is pricing a banking cycle the deposit base cannot fund.
Iron ore at 161.91 — up 70% from 95.08 — while India's core sector prints 2.3% YoY; the commodity is screaming capex, the output is whispering doubt.
Copper at a 78th-percentile $6.59/lb while India's core sector prints 2.3% — the industrial metal is pricing a capex cycle the domestic output data flatly refuses to confirm.
Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 68,714 while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — global equities are pricing a growth cycle the underlying economies have stopped delivering.
India VIX at a 6th-percentile 11.31 while FII flows swung ₹22,729 cr negative — the market is pricing serenity the foreign money is quietly exiting.
Airline passenger traffic at a 7th-percentile 35 million — down 9% in a month — while GST prints ₹2 lakh crore; one of these numbers is lying.
US 10Y at 4.68% — an 84th-percentile print, still climbing — while India's SIP accounts grow at a 2nd-percentile crawl; the carry trade that funds domestic equity optimism is thinning at both ends.
Nikkei reversing a five-month, 100th-percentile rally in a single session — while US 10Y holds 4.72% — is the carry-trade unwind the Nifty hasn't priced yet.
SIP inflows at ₹29,845 cr mask a 2nd-percentile account growth of 0.16 cr — India's retail equity story is deepening wallets, not widening participation.
Brent at $93 — rising 4 of 5 periods — while airline traffic hits a 7th-percentile 35 million; India's demand story has two completely different endings depending on which proxy you trust.
Euro Stoxx50 at a 100th-percentile 6,462 while falling five consecutive periods — global equities are celebrating a party the fundamentals stopped attending.

PMI Services at 57.5 — an 88th-percentile print, yet falling for the second period — while airline traffic sits at a 7th-percentile 35 million; India's services expansion is a headline the ground data is quietly contradicting.
Bank Nifty at a 96th-percentile 57,762 while FII equity flows reversed ₹22,729 cr in a single month — the market is pricing a banking boom the deposit base cannot fund.
Airline traffic at a 7th-percentile 35 million while e-commerce GMV halves to 12.4% YoY — India's affluent consumer is retreating, and the GST headline won't hide it for long.
Copper at an 80th-percentile $6.71/lb rising four of five periods while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — the metals market is pricing a global recovery the economy hasn't delivered.
India VIX at a 5th-percentile 10.6 while US 10Y yields hold at 4.64% — the market is pricing serenity India's airline and e-commerce data have already disproved.
US 10Y at 4.67% — an 84th-percentile yield — while global equities hit simultaneous all-time highs; someone is catastrophically wrong about the cost of capital.
SIP AUM at ₹16.64 lakh cr while new accounts grew at a 2nd-percentile 1.6% MoM — India's equity rally is being funded by deeper pockets, not wider participation.
US 10Y at 4.73% — an 85th-percentile yield rising three of five periods — while Nikkei and S&P sit at simultaneous all-time highs; the bond market and equity market cannot both be right.
Brent at $95.26 — a 5% surge in 30 days — hits India's import bill at ₹8,000 cr per $5 move while the RBI's inflation forecast of 4.6% was written at $90.
Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 64,325 — down 1,890 points in a session — while US 10Y hits 4.79%; global equity complacency is meeting its rate reckoning.
Airline passengers collapsed 9.5% MoM to a 7th-percentile 35M while GST hit ₹2.01 lakh crore — India's affluent are grounding themselves as mass consumption flies.
